📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:43 amNovember 17, 2026 at 11:43 am.

Industry observers note that seattle police already have a dog that sniffs out tech. Now they’ve got a piece of tech that looks like a dog.

The department’s Arson/Bomb Squad is now using a Spot robot from Boston Dynamics, bought with a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant that the Seattle City Council approved in April after a review of privacy and security risks. Bomb technicians can steer the robot from nearly a mile away to inspect suspicious devices, open doors and move possible explosives into safe containers, SPD said in a blog post last week.

Sources indicate that it’s a substantial upgrade for the squad, which has handled more than 600 calls so far this year. SPD’s main bomb robot is nearly 20 years old, weighs more than 100 pounds and rolls on tracks, and it can only be hauled around in the squad’s mobile workshop. Spot weighs under 100 pounds, climbs stairs and rides in a pickup truck that bomb techs drive daily.

SPD also spelled out what Spot won’t do.

According to recent reports, the robot will only be used for explosive threats in the city and at the port, and it won’t carry a weapon. SPD stated a weapon would go against Boston Dynamics’ rules for its robots. Spot’s 360-degree camera sends an encrypted live feed to the operator but doesn’t record or use facial recognition.

The only thing the robot does on its own is open a door, after an operator lines it up. As one bomb technician put it in SPD’s post, Spot will “be as dumb in 10 years as it is today.”.

It’s not the first time SPD has turned to a four-legged partner for tech-related work.

It has been revealed that nala, an electronic storage detection K9 — profiled by GeekWire in 2024 — is trained to smell a chemical compound used in making electronics. The Labrador retriever helps SPD’s Internet Crimes Against Children task force find hidden phones, hard drives and micro SD cards during warrant searches. Her handler, Det. Daljit Gill, told GeekWire at the time that Nala turns up a device human searchers missed about 30% of the time.

Spot appears decidedly less cuddly.

Industry observers note that boston Dynamics, maker of backflipping Atlas humanoids and other viral-video robots, first unveiled the robodog in 2015. A smaller, all-electric version followed a year later.

It has been revealed that the machines have long stirred dystopian unease. A 2017 “Black Mirror” episode featured killer robot dogs inspired by the tech giant’s designs. Still, Spot has turned up in friendlier settings: then-Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos walked one at the company’s MARS conference in 2018 — a scene described by GeekWire’s Alan Boyle as featuring the “anxiety-inducing” robot.

Police departments have embraced the robots, too. More than 60 bomb squads and SWAT teams in the U.S. and Canada use Spot, Bloomberg reported last year, including a regional bomb unit in Portland. New York police returned one in 2021 after public backlash, then brought the robots back two years later.

Back in Seattle, SPD’s bomb technicians see more potential uses down the road, according to the department’s post, including communicating and observing from a distance as part of de-escalation. For now, Spot’s job is limited to explosives.

And the robot won’t be getting a upcoming name, SPD noted, “because it is not a toy, or a dog, even though it kind of looks like both.”.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," remarked Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health. "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

Sources indicate that in the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our fresh, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

It has been revealed that product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand.".

Industry observers note that leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health, commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

Recent findings suggest that we continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in fresh product rolls out, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability.".

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results.

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

In a recent development, gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by latest product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Firm recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses.

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

It has been revealed that selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses.

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026.

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted EBIT represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), (vii) income tax (benefit)/expense, and (viii) interest income and interest expense. Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation is a non-GAAP measure, which excludes (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments, and is used as the numerator in computation of adjusted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation.

It has been revealed that we believe that adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that we include in net income/(loss) and net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation. We believe adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making.

Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation, should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to net income/(loss), basic and diluted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. Investors are encouraged to review the historical non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures. Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to ordinary shareholders, presented here may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data. We encourage investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.

The Teucrium fund gives investors double leveraged exposure to XRP.

Industry observers note that in the first quarter of 2026, RBC reported buying shares of the spot Bitwise XRP ETF for about $30,000. XRP was trading at $0.99 on Thursday.

The latest wave of 13F filings came out in November and covers the third quarter through Sept. 30. Goldman Sachs held about $144 million in XRP ETFs at the end of the third quarter, up from about $87 million at the end of the second quarter, according to its filing. The bank held shares of five spot funds from Franklin Templeton, Bitwise, Canary, Grayscale and 21Shares, and its crypto portfolio was worth $2.64 billion.

According to recent reports, italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed XRP fund holdings of $27.21 million. The bank held 712,319 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF, worth about $20.52 million, and it also opened a newly introduced position of 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF, worth about $6.7 million. Besides, trading firm Jane Street reported about $23.5 million in XRP funds.

Industry observers note that UBS and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund holdings of $1.91 million and $116,000, respectively. Bank of America held 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF, worth about $106,600.

Recent findings suggest that wells Fargo held about $11,000 in the Bitwise fund, and JPMorgan Chase held 539 shares of the same fund, worth about $9,000. National Bank of Canada held 330 shares of the Bitwise fund, worth about $5,500, and Bank of Montreal held REX-Osprey and ProShares Ultra XRP shares worth $4,300.

U.S. spot XRP ETFs held $1.08 billion in total assets as of Nov. 17, according to SoSoValue.

It has been revealed that form 13F filings only capture long positions in US-listed securities on a specific date. They don't show shorts, derivative hedges, intra-quarter trading or assets held outside the United States.

Breaking: Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1367 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation.
  • It has been revealed that most stablecoin rolls out promise a token that never moves.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to fresh institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

It has been revealed that eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

It has been revealed that most stablecoin rolls out promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

Recent findings suggest that according to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to fresh institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The company states R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

The project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery said the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it big" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

The model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the organization, cost nothing.

Sources indicate that the reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

Recent findings suggest that ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as new rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he said, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

In a recent development, the risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

The details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

It has been revealed that "Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let users redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

It has been revealed that in the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

The OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

Industry observers note that eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent tech giant, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

This background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU debuted earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

According to recent reports, the bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on company disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

For everyday users, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

The trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

Sources indicate that eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

Microsoft jabs at OpenAI and Anthropic, touting cheaper, customizable AI models of its own

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.
  • Industry observers note that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers.
  • “Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” mentioned Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the company’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:57 amNovember 17, 2026 at 12:33 pm.

Industry observers note that microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic, and it sells their AI models to its own customers. But another role was on full display during the organization’s Ignite keynote Tuesday: competitor.

“Simply stated, anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less,” mentioned Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s commercial business, during the opening keynote at the company’s annual conference for IT professionals and business customers in San Francisco.

In a recent development, jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, went further. “We’ve all seen Anthropic and OpenAI embrace documents, slides, and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration,” he said.

Sources indicate that the full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription. “That means that Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter,” Andreou noted.

Microsoft’s cost comparison: Andreou backed up the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees. It put Copilot at $30 for an “everyday” AI user, compared with $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude.

Recent findings suggest that for “advanced” customers of each firm’s agent tools, it demonstrated $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude. Most of the Claude figure is estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic’s $20 enterprise seat.

The numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads. They reflect enterprise pricing, which adds usage charges to a per-seat fee, not the flat monthly subscriptions that individuals pay for ChatGPT and Claude.

According to recent reports, partners and rivals: The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft’s core business. Last week it introduced new Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards that compete more directly with Office. The company is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects.

The companies’ products are also intertwined. Anthropic’s Claude for Microsoft 365, for example, lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks.

According to recent reports, the product has less than a tenth as many weekly users as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday, citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report said.

According to recent reports, fresh MAI models: Microsoft AI also released a new batch of its own MAI models, built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. It’s a notable stance, given that Microsoft still sells their models, too. On the same stage, CEO Satya Nadella announced that OpenAI’s GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

The lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday. Microsoft claims it delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price, on benchmarks Microsoft chose.

Sources indicate that microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2 Flash, a security model it says matches OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra on one benchmark at less than 2% of the cost per task. Other new models cover image editing, live speech and transcription.

It has been revealed that the other new business: MAI Licensed Weights. Companies can take a Microsoft AI model, customize it with their own data and run it in their own Azure environment, with help from Microsoft’s Frontier Tech giant consulting arm. AT&T used an earlier version of the program, Custom Models, to build a MAI model for 5G network analytics.

It’s the latest step in Microsoft’s push for what Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called “long term self-sufficiency,” which started with seven homegrown models at Build in June.

Sources indicate that keeping costs in check: The cost theme ran through the keynote. In a demo, Althoff showed Copilot building a keynote outline, a slide deck and a customer tracker for a retail conference, plus an agent he named Amelia to keep the work going.

The cost of his two-hour Sunday session: about 10,000 credits, or roughly $100. Althoff presented that as a bargain compared with the staff time it would have taken: “my team hits the ground running for NRF without me bothering them,” he remarked.

Sources indicate that microsoft is also selling tools to keep that bill in check. A new Agent 365 Business Analytics feature demonstrates business leaders what’s driving their AI spending and what they’re getting for it, and a companion Cost Management tool lets IT set spending policies and get alerts. Microsoft cited a McKinsey survey in which 93% of respondents reported exceeding their AI budgets.

In another notable announcement, Microsoft and Salesforce unveiled “Copilotforce,” bringing Salesforce customer data and actions into Copilot, Teams and Fabric. The Copilot plugin is available in preview.

Earlier, Nadella opened the keynote by addressing last week’s global Outlook outage.

According to recent reports, AI spending is shifting from giant training clusters toward smaller, rapidly built sites, and modular data centers are becoming a natural home for inference workloads. Power, cooling and memory supply now shape where tokens get generated as much as raw chip performance does.

Inference-first chipmakers want to capture that shift. Positron AI Inc., which raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation in September, builds inference appliances around commodity memory instead of scarce high-bandwidth memory. Inference has overtaken training as the force behind infrastructure buying decisions, according to Cameron McCaskill (pictured), head of sales and business development at Positron.

“We’re at a point where about two-thirds of the workloads being run through these AI infrastructures are inference versus one-third is training. And back in 2023, it was like 85% training, 15% inference,” McCaskill said. “So now you can see why inference is driving the economic decisions of how they’re going to build out their infrastructure.”.

McCaskill spoke with theCUBE Research’s Rebecca Knight and John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed inference overtaking training, Positron’s commodity-memory chip design and why low-power modular data centers suit inference. (* Disclosure below.).

Positron’s first-generation Atlas server ran on a programmable chip, and the manufacturer prepares to tape out its own silicon early next year for its Titan server. Oracle Corp. is bringing about 340 Atlas servers live in its cloud this quarter, McCaskill noted. A neocloud provider has also signed on for Atlas and committed to Titan. Positron’s central design choice was skipping high-bandwidth memory.

In a recent development, “Everyone else pretty much in the industry is using what’s called HBM or high bandwidth memory. It’s very limited in supply, very expensive,” McCaskill said. “We went with commodity memory.”.

In a recent development, that choice also keeps power low enough for air-cooled rooms. A single Positron server draws about 4,500 watts, and a full rack of Titan servers fits within 40 kilowatts, McCaskill explained. That footprint suits sites where operators can find a few megawatts of cheap power without heavy regulatory hurdles. For inference providers monetizing upcoming capacity, deployment speed is a massive part of the appeal, according to McCaskill.

“One of the groups of companies that we’re seeing a rise in right now and coming to us for product is these modular data centers, where they have a half megawatt or, 1 megawatt or 2.5 megawatt modular data center, and those can be deployed very rapidly,” McCaskill remarked. “And the goal of a lot of these inference players is I want to get from land and power to monetizable tokens within 90 to 120 days. And those modular data centers, coupled with our technology, can be a great solution.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Award Recognizes LG's Context-Aware Approach to In-Vehicle Information as Company Advances Validation with Global Automakers.

Sources indicate that SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) has won the 2026 Automotive News PACE Pilot Award for its UltraView Windshield Display, an in-vehicle display solution that indicates driving information and infotainment content across a large area of the windshield.

Recent findings suggest that presented by Automotive News, the PACE Pilot Award recognizes early-stage automotive innovations that are not yet commercialized but have demonstrated their potential through pilot programs. LG's win highlights its approach to organizing information within the driver's field of view.

Rethinking In-Vehicle Information Delivery.

Recent findings suggest that as vehicles add more digital functions and connected services, the amount of information presented to drivers keeps growing. With driving data, navigation, entertainment and vehicle controls often spread across multiple displays, drivers may need to shift their gaze between the road and different screens more frequently.

Industry observers note that rather than adding more screens or expanding display size, LG developed UltraView Windshield Display to rethink how, when and where information reaches the driver. The solution organizes information by importance and driving context, supporting a more intuitive driving experience. This reflects LG's broader vision for next generation automotive displays, which shifts the focus from individual display devices to a more integrated and context-aware information experience.

Bringing Context-Aware Information to the Windshield.

UltraView Windshield Display combines a compact, focus-free AR-HUD with LG's proprietary Hover HUD in a single optical system, presenting different types of visual data at distinct virtual distances. The AR-HUD projects driving-critical information, including vehicle speed, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) alerts, and navigation cues, at a far virtual distance aligned with the road. Its focus-free design reduces the difference in focal distance between the road and the projected image, so drivers can check information more naturally while keeping their eyes on the road. Meanwhile, the Hover HUD displays navigation, vehicle status, climate controls and multimedia content on a large virtual screen that appears closer to the driver.

Together, these two technologies allow UltraView Windshield Display to adjust screen size and information density to driving conditions, helping drivers access relevant information while minimizing unnecessary shifts in visual attention. Its compact design also gives automakers greater flexibility in cockpit design and display configuration.

Advancing Toward Real-World Vehicle Applications.

LG has been conducting vehicle-level proof-of-concept evaluations of UltraView Windshield Display with multiple global automakers, including premium brands in Europe and Asia. These collaborations include vehicle-level validation and sourcing discussions, and vehicle demonstrations and technology showcases have drawn further inquiries from automakers. Building on this progress, LG intends to further validate the technology for real-world vehicle applications and explore opportunities for future production programs.

Recent findings suggest that "Winning the Automotive News PACE Pilot Award recognizes our approach to rethinking how information is delivered inside the vehicle," noted Eun Seok-hyun, president of the LG Vehicle Solution Manufacturer. "We will build on this recognition by working closely with automakers to bring latest display experiences from innovation to real-world mobility.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the organization highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are at the moment trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data highlighted Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

According to recent reports, A Monero token crashed 99% on Friday after 5.2 million XMR1 tokens moved from a wallet tied to its creator, triggering a massive sell-off on Hyperliquid. The token, issued through crypto swap service Wagyu, plunged from around $494 to below $1 in 35 minutes. The wallet receiving the tokens sold enough to generate $13.22 million in USDC before converting the proceeds into 7,467 ETH.

Wagyu’s wallet security and the backing behind its wrapped Monero product are being questioned. And the sell-off also sent shockwaves through the Monero market, although native XMR remained a separate asset from the collapsing XMR1 market.

In a recent development, the incident began this morning when the account responsible for deploying XMR1 transferred tokens to a newly created wallet. Blockchain intelligence firm Bitquery identified three separate transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC. Two transactions moved 100,000 XMR1 each, followed by a much larger transfer of 5 million tokens.

The receiving wallet had been created that morning. It began selling shortly after receiving the tokens, overwhelming buyers on Hyperliquid’s order book. XMR1 had traded near $500 throughout the previous week. Its price then collapsed to about $1 within roughly 35 minutes, leaving holders with almost nothing.

According to recent reports, bitquery traced 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million. The remaining 4.83 million tokens stayed in the receiving wallet during its investigation. The sell-off also exposed how concentrated XMR1’s supply had been. Before the transfers, its deployer account still controlled 93% of the token’s supply.

Recent findings suggest that hyperliquid transfers require signatures from the account’s own key, rather than an ordinary trading API wallet. This means whoever authorized the transfers likely had access to the deployer’s main key. Whether someone stole that access or used it legitimately remains unknown.

Discover: The Best Token Presales.

The damage extended beyond traders watching XMR1 collapse on their screens. Bitquery matched the seller’s transactions against 388 accounts that purchased the dumped tokens. One buyer alone paid $3.56 million, while 27 large buyers accounted for 77% of the total proceeds.

The wallet did not leave the money sitting in USDC. It began moving funds through Hyperliquid’s bridge into Arbitrum shortly after selling.

XMR1 hack: 388 Hyperliquid buyers paid $13.50 million for a token that fell 99.8%https://t.co/k5ggHcH6Al.

It has been revealed that on Arbitrum, the wallet exchanged $13.22 million in USDC for 7,467 ETH through CoW Protocol. It then routed much of the Ethereum through Socket, Mayan, and Stargate. 6,810 ETH then arrived on Ethereum after those bridge transactions. Approximately 4,836 ETH landed in a newly created wallet that had not sent any funds onward.

Industry observers note that the investigation also identified 7,348 ETH across three wallets during its tracking window. That left a substantial amount of the proceeds sitting outside the original trading account.

The incident has put Wagyu’s bridge infrastructure under scrutiny. XMR1 represents Monero on Hyperliquid and is issued through Wagyu’s bridging service. People can move native XMR into the service and receive XMR1 for trading. They can also reverse the process to recover their Monero.

In a recent development, native XMR did not suffer the same collapse. Monero continued trading around $470–$482, while XMR1 lost virtually all its market value.

Holders now face a difficult question: Can they still exchange their remaining XMR1 for native Monero?

It has been revealed that the incident also comes weeks after Wagyu disclosed a separate data leak on October 28. Researchers identified exposed records potentially linking crypto deposits, Monero receiving addresses, and customer IP addresses.

Wagyu previously stated customer funds remained unaffected by that incident. No established connection links the October leak to Friday’s wallet transfers.

According to recent reports, the latest investigation also uncovered another potential concern. The same deployer account controls 99.97% of ZEC1, a separate token representing Zcash on Hyperliquid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 1:36 pmNovember 20, 2026 at 5:15 pm.

Seattle startup Aarden AI on Tuesday announced $8 million in new funding to grow its team and accelerate its work helping landowners evaluate potential uses for their properties and navigate deals with developers building data centers, clean energy projects, housing and other projects.

Founded last year, the organization claims its clients collectively own or manage approximately 14 million acres worldwide — nearly the land area of West Virginia. Aarden’s team remarked it has evaluated more than $500 million worth of land deals.

“But land markets remain opaque and manual with far too much friction. Finding the right site, and building trust with the right partners quickly, is more important than ever for our economy and our environment,” founder and CEO Danan Margason said in a statement.

The manufacturer combines data on hundreds of land attributes with historical market data and proprietary models to assess development suitability, valuation trends, ownership and community sentiment. Its tools and services also help developers identify sites and connect with landowners.

Aarden generates revenue through subscriptions to its technology, which includes AI-native data, models and investment tools, and through fees for services tied to specific deals or analyses.

According to recent reports, the new funding brings Aarden’s total investments to $12 million. Overture Ventures led the round, with participation from Madrona and Propeller Ventures. The startup previously raised $4 million in a round led by Planeteer in June 2025. The company has 13 employees and looks to nearly double in size over the next 12 months.

Margason mentioned he launched the business on the premise that while there have long been tools to support developers, landowners have been largely on their own to evaluate and optimize deals so they’re not taken advantage of or end up partnering with untrustworthy organizations.

One customer, timberland investment manager Resource Management Service, uses Aarden to evaluate whether tracts are best suited for continued timber production, conservation, solar development or other uses.

“Diligence that used to take months now produces investment-grade answers we can act on, and that is shaping how we manage value across our portfolio,” said Alex Hinson, president and CEO of Resource Management Service.

Other companies offering property research and analysis tools include Acres, which provides land data, valuations and due diligence tools, and Land id, which offers property insights and mapping tools.

Ben Eidelson, a partner at Stepchange Ventures, which participated in the startup’s first funding round, said the manufacturer is already having an impact.

“We now have the capability to make smarter decisions about land, optimizing for the outcomes that matter from conservation to the local economy,” Eidelson noted on LinkedIn.

Canton Coin Gets SEC "Digital Commodity" Label: Here's What the Two Prongs Actually Mean

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1317 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the SEC's Division of Corporation Finance called Canton Coin a digital commodity on November 3.
  • Industry observers note that the most important words in the SEC's Canton Coin letter aren't "digital commodity." They are the ones the staff put in front of that label: the conclusion holds "in reliance on the representations" Canton's lawyers made.
  • Sources indicate that on November 3, the Division of Corporation Finance's Office of Chief Counsel answered Canton Network's October 30 request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

It has been revealed that the SEC's Division of Corporation Finance called Canton Coin a digital commodity on November 3. The ruling rests on two representations, including the absence of a "central party.".

Industry observers note that the most important words in the SEC's Canton Coin letter aren't "digital commodity." They are the ones the staff put in front of that label: the conclusion holds "in reliance on the representations" Canton's lawyers made. The SEC didn't independently prove the network has no central party. It accepted a description and attached a conclusion to it.

Sources indicate that on November 3, the Division of Corporation Finance's Office of Chief Counsel answered Canton Network's October 30 request. The response came from Deputy Chief Counsel Jonathan A. Ingram and was addressed to the staff team of Ted Yu, Andrew Schoeffler and Mark Vilardo. The Division said it views Canton Coin as a "digital commodity" as the term is described in the SEC's March interpretation.

According to recent reports, it also stated it will not recommend enforcement action if Canton Coin is minted programmatically by Super Validators, Validators and application providers, as described in the request. That holds without registration under Section 5 of the Securities Act or Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, and it applies if the issuer relies on an opinion of counsel. The facts the staff relied on are laid out in the Canton Network's incoming letter.

According to recent reports, early coverage focused on the classification label. The more useful story, though, is how the staff got there.

Recent findings suggest that the staff pointed to two representations. The first is that Canton Coin is intrinsically linked to, and derives its value from, the programmatic operation of the Canton Network, along with supply and demand dynamics. Its value does not come from an expectation of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others.

That phrase echoes the Howey test, the long-standing U.S. framework for investment contracts. The prong asks a simple question: when someone holds this token, are they betting on a team's work, or on a network that runs by itself? On the facts presented, the staff's answer was the network.

It has been revealed that this is the more familiar half of the analysis, and most token projects argue some version of it. Because almost every issuer makes the same claim, the first prong carries less weight on its own, which is why the second one deserves a closer look.

The second representation is that the Canton Network has no "central party," as the March interpretation defines that term. In the SEC and CFTC's framework, a digital commodity belongs to a functional crypto system that has no central party overseeing participation or distributing rewards to consumers.

This prong is the one to watch, because Canton Coin is minted by Super Validators, Validators and application providers. Those are named roles in a structured network, so a skeptic could fairly ask whether the Super Validator tier looks like a central party in practice. The letter's answer rests on the word "programmatically": the minting follows protocol rules rather than anyone's discretion.

Sources indicate that legal commentators reading the March interpretation have also pointed out that it doesn't fully explain how the "central party" concept relates to its separate definition of decentralization. The Canton letter doesn't settle that either. It applies the term to one set of facts and stops there.

In a recent development, A no-action letter is narrower than it sounds. The Division itself claims the response states its position on enforcement action only and expresses no legal conclusion on the issues presented. It also says the positions rest on the representations in the request, and that different facts or conditions might lead to different conclusions.

In practice, that comes down to three points. First, the letter is staff-level guidance rather than a Commission vote. Second, it protects reliance on the specific arrangement described, not the token in every future circumstance. Third, if the representations change, the comfort can disappear.

For a firm, the letter is still valuable, since a written statement that staff won't recommend enforcement is a strong signal. Even so, it shouldn't be mistaken for a permanent legal classification. It is a snapshot of staff views based on facts someone else supplied.

The framework behind the letter is the Commission's March 17 interpretation, which the CFTC joined. It sorts crypto assets into five categories: digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, stablecoins and digital securities. Four of the five are generally treated as non-securities, and the securities analysis stays fact-specific for the rest.

The two documents do different jobs. The interpretation is a general map: it tells the market how the Commission thinks about categories and which features push an asset one way or the other. The Canton letter is an application. It takes a named token, tests it against the map's digital commodity category, and gives a case-specific enforcement answer.

According to recent reports, that sequence matters. The interpretation indicates what a digital commodity looks like, and the letter says that, if the facts are as represented, Canton Coin looks like one.

The practical lesson is about preparation. Canton's request framed its facts to fit the two prongs, and the staff responded in those terms. Projects hoping for similar treatment will likely follow the same template: document how value arises from network operation, and document why no single party oversees participation or distributes rewards.

Industry observers note that the harder test will come from tokens with more visible governance or a more active operating team. Those projects will have to explain why their structure doesn't amount to a central party, and the Canton letter doesn't say where that line sits.

Recent findings suggest that for now, the letter works best as an early data point rather than a final answer. The classification label drew the attention, but the representations behind it are what other projects will study. How the staff handles the next request, especially one with a messier governance story, will show whether the "no central party" prong is a narrow gate or a wide one.

Driving Clinical Development Leadership Through Global Expansion and Innovation.

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Founded in 1997, C&R Research (KOSDAQ: 359090) pioneered Korea's contract research organization (CRO) industry. With over 2,800 clinical projects, the manufacturer is expanding internationally while positioning AI and healthcare data as latest engines of growth.

From a Korean CRO Leader to a Global Clinical Development Partner.

It has been revealed that as drug development grows more complex and regulatory requirements vary across markets, integrated global capabilities have become essential. Through its operations in the United States, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, C&R Research has conducted multi-regional clinical trials (MRCTs) in more than 25 countries, supporting Korean companies in global trials and international companies in Korea and Asia.

With extensive experience in global regulatory affairs, including U.S. FDA requirements, C&R Research has strengthened its international presence. Global inbound contracts in 2025 reached 2.6 times the 2023 level. In 2026, the manufacturer was recognized among the Global Top 50 CROs and Asia-Pacific Top 25 CROs.

Combining Clinical Expertise with AI and Healthcare Data.

It has been revealed that AI and healthcare data are central to C&R Research's future competitiveness. As technology transforms clinical trial design, patient recruitment and data analysis, digital capabilities have become a key differentiator for CROs.

Recent findings suggest that C&R Research is enhancing its services by integrating AI and healthcare data with its clinical expertise. It is digitizing trial operations through eClinical solutions, exploring AI applications to improve efficiency, and expanding the use of healthcare data in clinical research. By leveraging the expertise of its affiliates Trial Informatics and Mediplexus, the firm aims to deliver integrated clinical development services powered by technology and data.

Sustainable Growth Through Global Reach and Innovation.

C&R Research plans to broaden its global network and strengthen its AI and healthcare data initiatives, while meeting the clinical quality and operational standards expected by global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across diverse markets.

Approaching its 30th anniversary in 2027, C&R Research aims to become a global CRO that pairs clinical expertise with technological innovation to help bring innovative therapies to patients faster and more efficiently.

It has been revealed that for more details contact Jisung Myeong (Brand Marketing Specialist/BMS) from C&R Research Inc. at [email protected] or visit https://www.cnrres.com/en/.

At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

The Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

Sources indicate that “So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more swiftly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

Sources indicate that “Several key Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

In a recent development, third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

According to recent reports, watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin (BTC) is facing renewed selling pressure as large holders continue to reduce their exposure, with on-chain data showing that whales have redistributed about $3.4 billion worth of the cryptocurrency over the past two weeks.

Notably, the largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has fallen nearly 13% over the past week. The decline extends its November losses, bringing its price to a three-month low.

According to analyst Ali Martinez, large entities have sold or redistributed 48,618 BTC, valued at approximately $3.4 billion, over the past two weeks.

In a recent development, “Whales are still reducing their exposure. The selling hasn’t stopped yet,” Martinez tweeted.

It has been revealed that the continued distribution suggests that major holders are yet to regain confidence in Bitcoin’s near-term prospects. With thousands of coins changing hands, the market faces the challenge of absorbing this supply without triggering further downward pressure.

Beyond whale activity, Bitcoin’s weekly performance is adding to concerns about the market’s strength.

Analyst Ted Pillows noted that the cryptocurrency has closed six consecutive weeks in the red, a pattern previously seen during bear markets. Trading below both moving averages further weakens its recovery prospects.

According to recent reports, “Along with that, Bitcoin failed to hold both the 200W EMA and 200W MA, which is a major sign of weakness. As long as BTC stays below these levels, sellers are in full control,” he wrote.

Meanwhile, several important price levels have given way, leaving Bitcoin vulnerable to another decline.

Mookie, an advocate at Bitget Wallet and ambassador at Dinari Global, highlighted the cryptocurrency’s failure to maintain successive support levels, warning that $57,700 could come into focus if buyers fail to regain control.

“If BTC can’t get back above $66.5K. we could see another drop toward the July low at $57.7K. But if buyers push it back above $66.5K we might finally see a bounce. Still not convinced we’re done dropping,” he noted.

According to recent reports, his comments put $66,500 at the center of Bitcoin’s immediate price outlook. Reclaiming that level could help buyers regain some momentum, while another rejection would leave the July low of $57,700 as a potential downside target.

Despite the prevailing bearish sentiment, some market observers believe Bitcoin could be approaching a turning point.

Gordon, founder of Crypto Crib and co-founder of Alphametrics, pointed to a potential inverse head-and-shoulders formation, suggesting that extreme pessimism could set the stage for a reversal.

According to recent reports, “All longs have been wiped out, sentiment is max bearish, and retail is going heavy short. This is where reversal happens,” he commented.

It has been revealed that an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern is a technical formation often associated with a potential bullish reversal after an extended decline. It typically consists of three troughs, with the middle one forming the lowest point.

Sources indicate that gordon’s assessment offers a contrasting view to the warnings from other analysts. He believes that widespread bearish positioning and the liquidation of leveraged long positions could create conditions for buyers to return.

However, the formation does not guarantee an immediate recovery. Bitcoin still needs enough buying interest to reverse its recent losses and reclaim key price levels.

At press time, BTC was trading at $59,299, down 5.40% over the past 24 hours.

‘Do not search Amazon’: Meta’s Muse now shops elsewhere by default

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.
  • Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.
  • The shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:36 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 9:45 am.

Two months after Amazon slammed the door on Muse, the AI agent has stopped knocking.

The shopping skill that guides Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, now tells it to “leave out Amazon unless the user asks for it,” according to the instructions Muse provides when asked. The instructions include a template brief for Muse’s browser that notes, “Do not search Amazon.”.

The change was spotted last week by Juozas Kaziukenas, founder of the e-commerce research firm Marketplace Pulse, who asked Muse for the text of its shopping skill and compared it with the version from the day before. He posted the before-and-after on Friday. GeekWire asked Muse for its shopping skill and got the same language.

“Amazon blocked Muse, so now Muse blocked Amazon,” Kaziukenas wrote on X.

Recent findings suggest that muse is also told not to name Amazon as a site to search in that browser brief, “even as an example,” unless the user asked for Amazon. The skill steers the agent to Walmart and Target for general goods, Best Buy for electronics, and Home Depot or Lowe’s for home improvement.

Recent findings suggest that for Muse customers, not much changes in practice. Amazon began blocking Muse in September, less than two weeks after Meta introduced the agent, showing anyone who tried to shop through it a message saying continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use. Kaziukenas noted any Amazon search would fail anyway because of the block.

It has been revealed that what’s fresh is that Meta appears to be going along with what Amazon asked for. When it began blocking Muse, Amazon said it had asked Meta to “remove Amazon from the experience.” Meta hadn’t said publicly how it would respond.

Meta didn’t respond to an inquiry about the change. An Amazon spokesperson stated the company had nothing to share.

Sources indicate that amazon objected that Muse didn’t identify itself when it browsed the site and appeared to capture and store customer credentials. Meta has noted Muse has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods. The standoff set off a broader debate over who owns the customer relationship when an AI agent does the buying.

Since then, both sides have kept moving. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada signed up for Muse in its first six weeks, Forbes reported, and Walmart, Best Buy, Sephora and Wayfair are among the retailers working with Meta on it.

The business stakes are high for Amazon. It generated more than $68 billion in advertising revenue last year, including sponsored products that appear as people browse its pages — ads a shopper might never see if an outside agent does the searching. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has remarked Muse will take a small cut of the transactions it handles.

Amazon has fought this battle before, suing Perplexity last November over the shopping agent in its Comet browser. It’s now pressing that case in part on the same Conditions of Use it cited in blocking Muse.

On Amazon’s earnings call last month, CEO Andy Jassy mentioned outside shopping agents aren’t making a meaningful dent in Amazon’s advertising business. “Few customers are doing much shopping this way yet,” he said, adding that the experience still isn’t great or more convenient than going straight to a retailer.

Jassy said Amazon expects to work with “horizontal agents,” general-purpose assistants like Muse, but believes its own Alexa for Shopping will be the main agent people use to shop Amazon. Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping in May, combining its Rufus shopping chatbot with the Alexa+ assistant.

It has since started letting some customers text Alexa to shop, much as people do with Muse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated aims to launch two latest XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

In a recent development, as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn prepares to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

According to recent reports, interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its plans to launch these two ETFs.

Roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

According to recent reports, unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

Sources indicate that A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

Industry observers note that notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

  • The global race for artificial intelligence is often perceived as a competition over who controls the largest data centers.
  • Sources indicate that this Chinese on-device AI unicorn has made efficiency the cornerstone of its overseas expansion strategy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, LISBON, Portugal, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This is a report from China Daily:.

The global race for artificial intelligence is often perceived as a competition over who controls the largest data centers. However, ModelBest offers a different perspective: how inclusive intelligence becomes depends on its accessibility and how widely it can be deployed.

Sources indicate that this Chinese on-device AI unicorn has made efficiency the cornerstone of its overseas expansion strategy. By November, its self-developed MiniCPM series of models had recorded more than 70 million downloads worldwide.

Industry observers note that "MiniCPM is not just one model. It is an entire family," Li Dahai, CEO of ModelBest, said at the Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal, which took place from Nov 9 to 12.

Each model serves a different form of intelligence, but they share one goal: higher intelligence density, faster speed, and lower cost on devices, he added.

That efficiency-first approach has been put to work abroad. In April, ModelBest revealed the Lao national model, LaoAI, which marked a landmark case of a Chinese AI company helping another nation build its own national AI foundation.

Built on the company's MiniCPM architecture and high-efficiency training methods, the system is integrated into G-Chat v2, the national government communications platform, and is used across government agencies and key industries.

According to recent reports, sovereign AI has largely been dominated by chipmakers, for whom sovereignty implies acquiring advanced computing power and constructing national data centers. LaoAI offers another path: instead of relying on a national supercomputing cluster, the team made multiple field research trips to Laos in the months leading up to the launch, building the system on high-efficiency model architecture rather than massive computing power.

The team also incorporated Lao culture and values into training through field research. The Lao translation capability of their model outperforms mainstream systems on international benchmarks.

Crucially, the underlying model and application programming interfaces are open to local developers. The complete model weights have been delivered to the Lao side, giving them control over everything from the model to the data.

Recent findings suggest that "Efficiency is the key to making large model technology available to everyone," Li said. "In the Lao national model project, an 8-billion-parameter system achieved world-leading Lao-language capability. This demonstrates that developing countries need not wait for top-tier computing power to benefit from AI," he added.

The significance is more developmental than commercial: countries of the Global South no longer need access to high-end computing capacity to step into the AI era.

In a recent development, the same principle applies to businesses. Making AI affordable for small and medium-sized enterprises is often touted but rarely realized. ModelBest's on-device approach changes that. When inference happens on the device, small businesses need neither cloud capacity nor data uploads to access usable AI.

It has been revealed that the technical foundation is what the firm calls the "Densing Law". The capability density of large models doubles roughly every 3.5 months, reducing the number of parameters needed for a given level of intelligence.

For such businesses, on-device AI is not merely cheaper: it is their first realistic chance to possess AI capability, with data on-premises, no per-inference fees, and no dependence on network coverage.

From sovereign models to on-device intelligence, ModelBest's international narrative aims to share the benefits of China's AI advancements with more countries, ensuring that each nation can develop its own AI capabilities in its own languages.

This direction echoes national policy: China's 2026 Government Work Report endorsed open-source AI ecosystems, and this year's World Artificial Intelligence Conference and the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit both advanced initiatives for a fair, open and sustainable global AI ecosystem.

For ModelBest, the overseas initiatives represent a microcosm of this broader vision. By prioritizing efficiency and openness, AI can be extended to countries and businesses that have been waiting on the sidelines.

Sources indicate that beyond expanding access, ModelBest is also rethinking how AI itself is built. The next step is to use AI to build AI itself.

"This is not only a technological change; it is a fundamental shift in how intelligence is produced," Li remarked.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it.
  • In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.
  • “It’s very important to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:48 EST / NOVEMBER 21 2026.

A sovereign AI factory is only as valuable as the companies that can actually get onto it. Across Europe, publicly funded AI factories are racing to give startups and small manufacturers supercomputer-class GPUs without pushing them into lock-in or loose data handling.

In Stuttgart, the HammerHAI AI factory is taking shape around a system from Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. using Nvidia Corp. Grace Blackwell chips. The center’s pitch leans as much on people as on processors, according to Bastian Koller (pictured), managing director of the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart.

“It’s very important to bring them there because everybody’s talking about AI, but we focus especially on SMEs and startups,” Koller said. “So some startups know what they want, some startups want to try and they need help and support.”.

Koller spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how HammerHAI avoids lock-in, its pragmatic approach to sovereignty and a concierge model that pairs each customer with a consistent contact. (* Disclosure below.).

Industry observers note that industrial people no longer want shell programming; they expect the look and feel of a hyperscaler, which raises fresh demands on security and access. The center has already worked with customers on existing systems while it waits on the new hardware, and several have produced success stories. Rather than holding onto them, it designs its services so workloads can leave, according to Koller.

Recent findings suggest that “The idea is to evolve the system and the services in a way that they can simply move from us to a hyperscaler or from hyperscaler back,” Koller remarked. “Because what we are doing is, we give them a boost, we push them forward.”.

That pragmatism extends to sovereignty itself. The Stuttgart center runs an ISO-certified environment with TISAX Level 3 certification for automotive work. Full independence, down to European chips, is not realistic in the near term, Koller explained.

It has been revealed that “We cannot now say, okay, come back in 10 years when we have a sovereign processor or a sovereign GPU or something like this,” Koller mentioned. “We have to look for the data.”.

According to recent reports, efficiency is part of the equation, too. The fresh system doubles the performance of its 3.2-megawatt predecessor at about 700 kilowatts, and the center reuses its waste heat. The bigger lesson is human: A concierge model pairs each customer with a consistent contact, according to Koller.

Recent findings suggest that “We learn more how the people are working and thinking, to be honest,” Koller stated. “… We can build up a system which is highly fancy, whatever there, nobody will use it because we never thought about what the user needs.”.
